feature: op6893 DPMAIF downlink: attempts to make the modem deliver a packet, and the fault that stops it

image.note: one flash reported a fastboot failure after 'Writing boot OKAY'; the device was re-flashed with the same image and booted, and the release string was read back over Wi-Fi SSH

uplink_payload_format.finding: the DPMAIF uplink payload is the bare IP packet; the lhif_header belongs to the CCIF/CLDMA paths. Per-packet metadata lives in the message descriptor: channel_id is the CCMNI index (struct ccci_rpc_queue_mapping documents net_if as 'ccmni index'), network_type comes from the RIL's SIOCSNETTYPE and defaults to 0.
uplink_payload_format.queue_mapping: port_rpc.c ccci_rpc_remap_queue(): lhif_q 2 (LHIF_HWQ_AP_UL_Q0) maps to MD_HW_NORMAL_Q = 0, lhif_q 3 maps to MD_HW_IMS_Q = 3. Both values were observed on hardware, so neither the CCMNI index nor the queue can be hardcoded.

what_was_tried.attempt: IPv4 ICMP echo to the PDN's DNS server, source = the assigned PDP address
what_was_tried.result: uplink descriptor consumed (sent=1 done=1 irqs=1 err=0), no downlink entry, AO_DL_PIT_STA2 write index stayed at its initial value

what_was_tried.attempt: IPv6 ICMP echo to the PDN gateway, and to a public IPv6 resolver
IPv6 ICMP echo to the PDP's own address

what_was_tried.result: no difference; the write index never moved

what_was_tried.attempt: vendor notification of the AP PIT index (PD_UL+0xAC = 0xff then PD_MD_MISC+0x1C = bit 0, after the same-board drv2_dl_add_apit_num tail)

modem_fault.what: the modem takes a fatal exception while uplink data flows with the downlink ring armed
modem_fault.record: offender=MCU ex_type=49 class=fatal pc=0x91831724 lr=0x91831764 cause=0x40800824 status=0x6002, addr varies between runs (0x86fc4c4b, 0xb294f00e, 0x32b4f00f)
modem_fault.reproducibility: fixed pc, within three uplink start/stop cycles, twice on separate boots
isolation: downlink ring alone, started and stopped four times: modem stays up, no exception
uplink ring alone, started and stopped four times, including sending a packet: modem stays up, no exception
downlink ring armed plus uplink start/data/stop: exception appears
one uplink packet with the downlink armed survived once, so the fault is not triggered by the first packet deterministically
not_prevented_by: waiting for the uplink engine to report idle before tearing the ring down (PD_UL_DBG_STA2 bits 31:26, the same-board check)
refusing ul_stop while the downlink ring is running
modem_fault.consequence: the driver now refuses to run both rings at once; this is a mitigation, not a fix. The root cause is on the modem side and needs evidence the AP cannot obtain.

not_proven: whether the uplink packets reach the network at all: descriptor consumption proves the transport layer took them, not that the modem forwarded them
whether the modem writes downlink entries when it does receive something, because no packet was ever received
the root cause of the modem fault
fragment reassembly and delivery to the network stack: the drain still only keeps a bounded head and recycles buffers

tooling_added.tx_hex: sends an exact caller-supplied byte string up the uplink, so the packet can be built and checksum-verified on the host instead of in the driver
tooling_added.peek_poke_reset: bounded register window over the five mapped blocks, refused while a ring runs, plus the vendor's AO/PD reset sequence; these turned each register hypothesis from a five-minute flash into seconds
tooling_added.packet_builder: modem-ip6-probe.py builds and self-verifies IPv4 and IPv6 echo requests (in the non-git build workspace)
tooling_added.wifi_ssh: ssh-wifi.sh reaches the device over Wi-Fi when the USB gadget drops off the bus; the device stayed reachable at 10.65.84.170 during both USB disappearances
